extracted.intended_audience: SymPy documentation writers and project contributors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for creating SymPy narrative docs and docstrings (API docs) using Sphinx/reStructuredText or MyST Markdown, including formatting, tone, math and code conventions, and where content should live.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and value of documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation should teach users and contributors how to use the project, how to contribute, and the standards of conduct within the open source community; aim for completeness and clarity since incomplete/confusing docs are a common problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation is one of the most highly valued aspects of an open source project and should support SymPy's mission to be a full-featured open source CAS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation source formats and toolchain
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation is generated from docstrings in source code and narrative files in doc/src, written in reStructuredText extended by Sphinx (with certain enabled extensions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the formats required by the processing tools (reStructuredText, Sphinx, and enabled extensions like autodoc, graphviz, mathjax). The style guide supersedes some recommendations from those tools; see tool docs for advanced features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use only supported Sphinx/extensions features
rubrics_metrics.description: Everything supported by the listed processing tools is available for use, but the style guide supersedes any recommendations made by those documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of the specific Sphinx extensions enabled (autodoc, graphviz, mathjax, linkcode, numpydoc, sphinx_math_dollar, matplotlib plot_directive) and use features accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate placement of content (types of documentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose the correct location for content: SymPy Website for advertising/overview; docs.sympy.org for tutorials and technical module docs; docstrings in source for API reference; wiki for editable high-level developer docs and release notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative documentation belongs in doc/src (Sphinx RST or Markdown). API/reference documentation belongs in docstrings and is pulled into Sphinx with autodoc. The wiki is for high-level or community-edited pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative vs API documentation separation
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative documents are standalone reST files in doc/src and should contain extensive/tutorial material not centered on a single API reference; reference documentation should go in docstrings and be pulled into RST with autodoc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your documentation is not API documentation it belongs in a narrative page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markdown usage limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative documentation can be written in reStructuredText (.rst) or Markdown (.md) via MyST; Markdown is only supported for narrative documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Docstrings must continue to use RST syntax. Any style guidance not specific to RST still applies to Markdown documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docstring purpose and doctest requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Docstrings explain the API of classes/functions and include examples called doctests which are tested as part of the test suite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doctest examples must produce the output they declare; docstrings are automatically included in Sphinx-generated docs, so format them so Sphinx renders them correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Math formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Text meant to appear as LaTeX math should be written between dollar signs: $math$; MathJax renders math in HTML builds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use $...$ for math. The HTML build will show invalid math as an error on the page; PDF builds (CI) will fail if LaTeX is invalid, so check final rendering.

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeX in docstrings and recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a docstring has any LaTeX, make it 'raw' and consider using SymPy's latex() function when unsure. Avoid unnecessary \left, \right, and unnecessary braces {}; use whitespace to improve readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show preferred simple forms (e.g., \int \sin(x), dx) and warn that PDF builds will fail on invalid LaTeX. Always check the final rendering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code formatting and inline code vs math
rubrics_metrics.description: Text that should be printed verbatim (code) should be surrounded by double backticks (``like this``). If the sentence is discussing mathematics use LaTeX; if discussing SymPy implementation use code formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a variable appears both as code and math: if it's a parameter listed by itself, italicize as a parameter; if in a larger code expression use double backticks. Use RST cross-reference syntax when referring to other SymPy functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameter and variable formatting precedence
rubrics_metrics.description: Variables listed in the parameters after a function name should be italicized (Sphinx emphasis) when referred to in prose; parameters take precedence over code formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a variable is code but also a parameter written by itself, render as italics; if a parameter appears in a larger code expression render with double backticks. If a variable is only code use double backticks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-referencing functions
rubrics_metrics.description: References to other functions in SymPy should use Sphinx cross-reference reStructuredText syntax rather than parameter or code formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the Cross-Referencing section for exact syntax (ensures proper linking in generated docs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Headings and heading adornments
rubrics_metrics.description: Section headings in reStructuredText are created by underlining/overlining the title with punctuation characters; SymPy suggests a convention for adornment characters for heading levels (=== overline for title, --- heading 1, --- heading 2, ^^^ heading 3, ~~~ heading 4, """ heading 5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the suggested convention to maintain consistent document structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spelling and punctuation conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: All narrative writing follows American spelling and punctuation standards; commas go inside quotation marks and function/term spelling should follow the SymPy function name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If ambiguous, refer to the spelling of the actual SymPy function (e.g., 'Chebyshev' rather than alternative transliterations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of headings
rubrics_metrics.description: Title case capitalization is preferred in all SymPy headings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'What is Symbolic Computation?' as a heading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and voice preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Write in the present tense, use first-person inclusive plural ('we'), prefer the generic 'you' or 'the reader'/'the user', use gender-neutral pronoun 'they', and avoid extraneous/belittling/unwelcoming or judgmental language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid words like 'obviously', 'easily', 'simply', 'just', and phrases like 'That is wrong.' Use friendly phrasing like 'A common mistake is…' and avoid phrases like 'we just have to do one more thing.'

rubrics_metrics.name: SymPy-specific deviations from other standards
rubrics_metrics.description: SymPy does not follow PEP 257 or the www.python.org documentation recommendations in all cases; follow the SymPy Documentation Style Guide where it differs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When in doubt between PEP 257/python.org docs and the SymPy style guide, prefer the SymPy style guide for SymPy documentation.
